memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports mild dizziness on turning head, able to perform ADLs independently.
cognition: Mini-Cog 4/5 (negative).
falls: 0 falls in last 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 9 seconds (normal).
medicines: 0 regular.
mood: affect appropriate, denies low mood.
carers: none.
goal: "I want to stop the spinning feeling and get back to work."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg twice daily
meclizine 25 mg as needed for vertigo
levocetirizine 5 mg once daily
cetirizine 10 mg at bedtime

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Dix-Hallpike test: positive on right side, transient torsional nystagmus lasting <15 sec. Consistent with benign positional vertigo (right posterior canal).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: No known drug allergies. Reports mild rash to sulfa antibiotics in childhood, resolved.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: vertigo episodes reduced to once weekly, still avoids sudden head turns.
cognition: Mini-Cog 4/5 (negative).
falls: 0 falls; gait slightly cautious; timed up-and-go 10 seconds (normal).
medicines: 4 regular (betahistine, meclizine PRN, levocetirizine, cetirizine).
mood: reports occasional frustration with dizziness.
carers: none.
goal: "I’d like to have fewer dizzy spells and feel safe at work."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg twice daily
meclizine 25 mg as needed (reduce to once daily if needed)
levocetirizine 5 mg once daily
cetirizine 10 mg at bedtime (continue)

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 6.0 x10^9/L, Hb 13.0 g/dL, Plt 205 x10^9/L, Eosinophils 0.4 x10^9/L.
TSH 2.0 mIU/L, FT4 1.3 ng/dL.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Audiometry (pure tone): bilateral hearing thresholds within normal limits (0-25 dB HL) across 250-8000 Hz. No conductive or sensorineural loss.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: vertigo now rare (<1/month), able to climb ladders at pharmacy.
cognition: Mini-Cog 4/5 (negative).
falls: 0 falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 4 regular (betahistine, meclizine PRN, levocetirizine, cetirizine).
mood: stable.
carers: none.
goal: "I want to stay symptom‑free and continue my job without worry."

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 5.8 x10^9/L, Hb 12.9 g/dL, Plt 212 x10^9/L, Eosinophils 0.5 x10^9/L (slight rise).
TSH 2.2 mIU/L, FT4 1.2 ng/dL.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Message via clinic app: ‘I’ve been getting hives almost daily, especially after night shifts. Antihistamines help but I still wake up itchy.’

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Refer to Dermatology, Sunrise Specialty Centre, for evaluation of chronic urticaria unresponsive to standard antihistamines. Consider allergy workup and possible biologic therapy.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Dermatology review: chronic urticaria likely autoimmune. Recommend continuing levocetirizine 5 mg OD, add omalizumab 150 mg SC every 4 weeks if symptoms persist. Return for review in 8 weeks.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg twice daily
meclizine 25 mg as needed
levocetirizine 5 mg once daily
cetirizine 10 mg at bedtime (continue)
Consider omalizumab pending insurance approval.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked with Dr Nandini Kulkarni for 2026-08-15 10:30 AM. Patient to bring symptom diary.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: vertigo absent for 3 months; works full shifts without restriction.
cognition: Mini-Cog 4/5 (negative).
falls: 0 falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 8 seconds.
medicines: 4 regular (betahistine, meclizine PRN, levocetirizine, cetirizine).
mood: reports improved quality of life.
carers: none.
goal: "I want to stay free of vertigo and hives, and keep working as a pharmacy assistant."
